findings.status: predicted, confirmed, resolved in the skill
findings.what: A grilled project with tests/ and a .venv but no root manifest derives an empty test_command, and the rendered adapters/test fails closed with a TODO on every run — the gate certifies nothing and every task parks at the merge gate.
findings.resolution: Per the operator decision of 2026-09-11 this is a gap in the maestro-setup skill, not in maestro/cli.py and not a DuetFlow chore. ~/.claude/skills/maestro-setup/SKILL.md gained Step 1a: verify the suite runs, write the smallest manifest that declares what is already true, re-run the derivation, and verify the RENDERED adapter at the end of Step 6. No pyproject.toml was hand-added ahead of the skill.
findings.evidence: duetflow 521822b adds pyproject.toml; adapters/test renders TEST_COMMAND non-empty and `echo '{}' | ./adapters/test` returned {"pass": true, ...} exit 0.

findings.status: new, recorded by operator decision, NOT fixed
findings.what: _derive_repo_facts builds the Python test command as (git_root/'.venv'/'bin'/'python3').resolve(strict=False). .venv/bin/python3 is a symlink to the system interpreter, so resolve() walks it OUT of the virtualenv: the derived command is /usr/bin/python3.11 -m pytest -q. The venv is bypassed entirely.
findings.why_it_matters: It passes on this host only because the system interpreter happens to have pytest installed. The first DuetFlow dependency that lives only in .venv turns every gate run into a collection error, and the failure reads as the task's fault.

findings.what: On a repo with no .orchestrator/ directory at all, a single `maestro init` run reports '.orchestrator/state.json already exists and differs' and writes a spurious state.json.new containing {}. Nothing pre-existed: init's own no-op supervised loop check creates state.json part-way through the run, and the scaffolding step then treats its own output as a pre-existing file it must not clobber.
findings.why_it_matters: A first-time install ends with an unexplained .new file and a diff the operator is invited to merge. The correct action is to delete it, and nothing says so.
findings.evidence: The init transcript's first block; .orchestrator did not exist in the pre-flight listing minutes earlier.

findings.what: init proposes .gitignore.new — a 7-line file that REPLACES the project's curated 56-line .gitignore rather than appending to it. The proposed file drops the ignores for config.yaml, *.token, tokens/, *.db and data/.
findings.why_it_matters: DuetFlow's invariant I9 is 'no token, secret, or config.yaml is ever written to the repo', and .gitignore is the filesystem half of enforcing it. An operator who merges the .new file as offered deletes that enforcement on a fresh install, silently, while doing what the tool suggested.

findings.status: new, fixed in the skill, NOT fixed in maestro
findings.what: The setup rehearsal only cleared F1 because DuetFlow happened to carry a hand-added no-op test (tests/test_smoke.py, `def test_skeleton(): assert True`, committed 27752a2 before the grill). A project in the state grill-with-docs actually leaves — CONTEXT.md, docs/adr/, docs/PLAN.md and nothing else — has no tests/ at all, so Step 1a's own precondition ('the repo has a real test suite') would not have fired and F1 would have recurred in full.
findings.second_order: Making Step 1a fire on manifest-absence alone is NOT sufficient. Measured on a scratch repo 2026-09-11: with a pyproject.toml carrying [tool.pytest.ini_options] and no tests/ (or an empty tests/), _derive_repo_facts returns a NON-EMPTY test_command, so the skill's own derivation check passes — but pytest exits 5 ('no tests ran'), which the rendered adapters/test reports as {"pass": false}. Every task then parks at the merge gate with a summary reading `no tests ran`, which an implementing agent reads as its own failure and tries to fix inside its own diff. That is a worse failure than F1's TODO, because it does not look like a setup problem.
findings.why_it_matters: The pilot's F1 'resolved' verdict was contingent on an accident of this scratch project. Without the hand-added test, the rehearsal would have ended with a broken gate either way.
findings.evidence: _derive_repo_facts on a docs-only git repo -> test_command ''. Same repo + minimal pyproject -> '<repo>/.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest -q'. `python3 -m pytest -q` with testpaths=['tests'] and no tests dir -> exit 5; with an empty tests/ -> exit 5, 'no tests ran'.
findings.resolution: ~/.claude/skills/maestro-setup/SKILL.md Step 1a rewritten: the trigger is now 'init would derive an empty test command', not 'there is a suite but no manifest'; it states that grill-with-docs leaves no manifest and no tests and that this is the NORMAL case; it splits into Case A (suite exists) and Case B (greenfield), where Case B must write the manifest AND seed one honest test that asserts something real (never `assert True`) AND report that the gate certifies only that AND put the placeholder's replacement into the first roadmap task's notes; and the step now verifies the suite exits 0 with a test collected, calling out exit 5 by name. The pre-flight bullet and the Step 6 assertion were updated to match. maestro/cli.py is unchanged — P00 characterises.

findings.what: maestro's scaffolding writes adapters/, profiles/ and systemd/ into the repo ROOT. For a Python project that is three extra top-level directories, and setuptools' flat-layout package discovery refuses to build when it sees more than one: `error: Multiple top-level packages discovered in a flat-layout: ['systemd', 'profiles', 'duetflow', 'adapters']`. `pip install -e .` fails outright.
findings.why_it_matters: Any Python project onboarded onto maestro that later tries to become installable hits this, and the error names maestro's directories without naming maestro. An unattended agent whose task is 'make the CLI runnable' would most plausibly resolve it by deleting or moving maestro's own scaffolding. Adjacent to F4: both are cases of init writing into a shared root namespace as though it owned it.
findings.evidence: duetflow 979727d: `.venv/bin/pip install -e .` exit 1 with the message above. Resolved in the project by declaring `[tool.setuptools] packages = ["duetflow"]` — a workaround in the project, not a fix in maestro.
